_description: $50k Roth conversion with NO Taxable account, verifying hybrid sourcing falls back to withholding tax from the conversion itself (IRS Form 1099-R Box 4 mechanic). Single filer, FL, age 60.
_rationale: Single age 60, FL (no state tax), Trad $500k, Roth $0, NO Taxable. One-time $50k conversion. Federal tax on $50k single 60: std ded ~$15.75k → ~$34.25k taxable → ~$4-5k federal tax. Under hybrid: no Taxable + no RMD-excess (age 60), so the full conv tax is withheld from the conversion (rothConversionTaxWithheld ≈ $4-5k). The conversion still executes the full $50k gross — rothConversionGross = $50k, withdrawalFromTraditional = $50k. The Roth deposit (computed in applyCashFlow as gross − withheld) lands at ~$45k. This is the core hybrid behavior: instead of capping to $16k (prior PR), the conversion proceeds at the user's requested size with mathematically suboptimal but practical self-funded tax.
name: Roth Conversion — Self-Funded (no Taxable)
